canonical_statement: The review assessed safety outcomes of SGLT2 inhibitors in randomized trials that prespecified heart failure in their inclusion criteria.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In this meta-analysis, we assessed the safety of SGLT2i in the trials that prespecified heart failure in their inclusion criteria.

canonical_statement: The systematic-review protocol was reported as registered under CRD 42022303987.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A protocol for this systematic review was registered on PRESPRO (CRD: 42022303987).

canonical_statement: The authors searched EMBASE, MEDLINE via PubMed, and Cochrane CENTRAL via Ovid for randomized controlled trials of SGLT2 inhibitors in heart-failure patients, with all databases searched on April 14, 2022.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The databases EMBASE (Embase.com), MEDLINE via PubMed, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials via Ovid were searched for randomized control trials of SGLT2i on heart failure patients.

canonical_statement: No additional search filters or limits were applied beyond the adapted RCT filters, and the complete database strategies were supplied in Appendix A.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: No additional filters or limits were applied. The search was subsequently mapped to the subject headings and syntax of the other selected databases.

canonical_statement: Duplicate records were removed manually in EndNote and then further deduplicated in Covidence.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Duplicate studies were removed manually in EndNote ... and then loaded into Covidence, which identified additional duplicates.

canonical_statement: Two authors independently screened titles/abstracts and reviewed full texts in duplicate, resolving eligibility disagreements by consensus.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Following title and abstract screening, the full text was reviewed independently and in duplicate in Covidence by two authors (AY and SN) to determine full eligibility.

canonical_statement: The main analysis focused on randomized controlled trials of heart-failure patients receiving an SGLT2 inhibitor and excluded trials with fewer than 300 participants; observational studies, retrospective studies, reviews, and letters were excluded.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Smaller clinical trials with <300 participants. Phase 2 and 3 clinical trials, observational studies, retrospective studies, reviews, and letters were excluded.

population.label: Heart-failure patients in randomized SGLT2 inhibitor trials

canonical_statement: The primary outcome was serious adverse events, defined as life-threatening events, death, hospitalization or prolonged hospitalization, significant or persistent disability, or birth defect/congenital anomaly.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The primary outcome was the incidence of SAEs. SAEs were defined as any medical event that is life-threatening or results in death, requires inpatient hospitalization or prolongation of existing one, causes significant or persistent disability, or is a birth defect/congenital anomaly.

outcome.definition: Life-threatening event, death, hospitalization/prolonged hospitalization, significant or persistent disability, or birth defect/congenital anomaly.

canonical_statement: Exploratory safety outcomes included bone fracture, ketoacidosis, genital infection, urinary tract infection, volume depletion, venous thromboembolism, amputation, hypoglycemia, acute kidney injury, hyperkalemia, hypotension, and symptomatic hypotension.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Other outcomes were explored such as bone fracture, ketoacidosis, genital infections, urinary tract infections (UTIs), volume depletion, venous thromboembolism (VTE), amputations, hypoglycemia, acute kidney injury (AKI), hyperkalemia, hypotension, and symptomatic hypotension.

canonical_statement: Pooled effects were summarized as odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals using RevMan 5.4.1 and a random-effects model; a 95% confidence interval including 1 was treated as non-significant.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Two independent analyses were performed using odds ratio (OR) with a 95% confidence interval (CI) to summarize the data.

canonical_statement: The authors performed a sensitivity analysis adding trials with fewer than 300 participants and a second sensitivity analysis according to heart-failure phenotype by excluding the HFpEF-focused trials.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Another analysis was performed after including phase 4 trials that recruited <300 patients. We complemented these analyses with a sensitivity analysis according to the type of HF (HFrEF or HFpEF).

canonical_statement: The PRISMA flow diagram reported 1,813 records identified, 424 duplicates removed, 1,389 records screened, 1,375 records excluded, 14 reports assessed for eligibility, 9 reports excluded, and 5 studies included.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Studies included in review (n = 5)

canonical_statement: Five trials with 15,987 participants were included: 7,994 participants received an SGLT2 inhibitor and 7,993 received placebo; two trials enrolled HFrEF, two focused on HFpEF, and one enrolled patients recently hospitalized for heart failure.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Five trials containing 15,987 participants (7994 received an SGLT2i and 7993 received a placebo) met our inclusion criteria and were included.

population.label: Five randomized controlled trials of patients with heart failure or recent heart-failure hospitalization

canonical_statement: The review reported that about 80% of included participants had left ventricular ejection fraction below 50%.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: However, about 80% of the participants had a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of <50%.

population.label: Included review population; approximately 80% had LVEF <50%

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Two trials compared dapagliflozin to placebo ... two compared empagliflozin to placebo ... and one trial compared Sotagliflozin to placebo.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that SGLT2 inhibitors were associated with fewer serious adverse events in heart-failure patients with reduced and preserved ejection fractions, but with higher rates of genital infection, urinary tract infection, and hypotension.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: SGLT2i are associated with a lower incidence of SAEs ... They are associated with a higher incidence of genital infections, UTIs, and hypotension with no significant difference in other safety outcomes.

canonical_statement: The authors identified differences in baseline age, pump function, and follow-up duration across trials as potential sources of heterogeneity.

canonical_statement: Sotagliflozin inhibits both SGLT1 and SGLT2, whereas dapagliflozin and empagliflozin inhibit SGLT2, introducing pharmacologic heterogeneity within the pooled class.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Third, sotagliflozin inhibits SGLT1 and SGLT2 while dapagliflozin and empagliflozin only inhibit SGLT2.

canonical_statement: The review could not perform safety analyses stratified by diabetes status because the included trials did not report safety outcomes by diabetes status.
